column1: # What this project has admitted it owes.
# One row per obligation. Presence here is admission; removing a row escapes
# to a person, because admitted obligations may not quietly decrease within an
# epoch. Whether a row APPLIES is recomputed on every run from its `applies`
# command and never stored, so an obligation goes dormant when the grounded
# state stops making it applicable, and comes back when it does — nothing here
# can waive it. Whether it is DISCHARGED is the evidence command's verdict:
# exit 0 holds, 1 fails, 2 cannot examine. Its output is the coverage report.
# obligation
# class:    INFO ADVISORY TASK_BLOCKING RELEASE_BLOCKING AUTHORITY_BLOCKING
# pathway:  deterministic witness corroborated probabilistic unknown
#           (probabilistic is advisory only and may not carry a blocking class)
# grounds:  probe predicate(s) from probes.tsv the applicability rests on, or -
# The first obligation every plugin owes: each lifecycle moment it has taken a
# stance on is wired the way the stance says, and no moment is wired without a
# stance. Dormant while the project ships no hooks.json. The evidence below is
# a HOLD, not a check: it exits 2, so the day this project ships hooks the row
# reads UNKNOWN and blocks with what to write, and can never pass by having
# nothing to examine. Replace it with a checker over this project's own stance
# table when there is one.
lifecycle_wired
column5: printf 'this project ships hooks and has no stance table; write lifecycle.tsv and name a checker over it here\n'; exit 2
column7: a moment with nothing at it is a completion nobody checks, and a floor that does not run reports nothing
